{{Quote|Petite and athletic... she had green, mischief-filled eyes and a smile diabolic enough to suggest she'd be a lot of fun in a firefight|A description of Altamik|<ref name="Vortex">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Vortex]]''</ref>}}
'''Turi Altamik''' was a [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] of the [[New Jedi Order]]. She fell prey to a [[Force psychosis]] in [[44 ABY]], and the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] demanded the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] Order to turn her over, laying [[Siege of the New Jedi Temple|siege]] to the [[New Jedi Temple|Jedi Temple]]. However, she and the other psychotic Knights soon recovered, and after examination by [[Doctor/Legends|Doctor]] [[Thalleus Tharn]], were pronounced sane, forcing the government to lift the siege. Later, Altamik took part in the [[Raid on Detention Center 81|rescue]] of [[Valin Horn|Valin]] and [[Jysella Horn]] from [[Galactic Alliance Security]] [[Galactic Alliance Security Detention Center 81|Detention Center 81]].

==Biography==
In [[44 ABY]], Altamik came down with a [[Force psychosis|psychosis]], brought on by the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] being [[Abeloth]], which made her believe that everyone she knew had been replaced by impostors. Altamik escaped the [[New Jedi Temple|Jedi Temple]], and although she was soon captured by the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]], she was caught on [[Holocamera/Legends|holocam]] by [[Journalist/Legends|journalist]] [[Javis Tyrr]].<ref name="Allies" />

[[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Cilghal]] drew up a report that went into detail about the psychosis in Altamik and fellow Jedi Knight [[Kunor Bann]], believing the rate of Jedi succumbing to the psychosis was accelerating. The [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]], meanwhile, ordered that the Jedi release Altamik and [[Sothais Saar]]&mdash;a [[Chev]] Jedi who had recently succumbed to the same psychosis&mdash;to government custody. Acting [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] [[Kenth Hamner]] refused the directive, which resulted in [[Chief of State (Galactic Alliance)|Chief of State]] [[Natasi Daala]] ordering a [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Siege of the New Jedi Temple|siege]] of the Jedi Temple. When the [[Jedi High Council (New Jedi Order)|Jedi Council]] sent Hamner's [[Aide/Legends|aide]], [[Kani Asari]], out to negotiate with the Mandalorians, [[Belok Rhal]], the [[Commander/Legends|commander]] of the Mandalorian siege, noted that Kani was neither Altamik nor Saar and shot her on sight, [[Death/Legends|killing]] her instantly. Despite the violence, the Jedi still refused to turn over the two psychotic Knights.<ref name="Allies" />

Before long, however, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] completed [[Mission to the Maw|his mission]] to defeat Abeloth, apparently killing her and thus instantly ending Altamik's psychosis.<ref name="Allies" /> However, Luke soon discovered that Abeloth had not been killed and suspected that by being wounded and weakened she had lost her control over the Jedi Knights' minds.<ref name="Vortex" />

Altamik and Saar were brought out before to the Jedi Temple steps, where Daala's chosen [[Doctor/Legends|doctor]], [[Thalleus Tharn]], examined them. Tharn pronounced them to be cured, and Daala lifted the siege, although she refused to release the Horn siblings from [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]]. Soon thereafter, Altamik was one of many formerly psychosis-afflicted Jedi to participate in the [[Raid on Detention Center 81|rescue]] of [[Valin Horn|Valin]] and [[Jysella Horn]]. She piloted a disguised [[Cygnus-7 armored transport]] which served as "Team Saav'etu"'s and "Team Solo"'s primary escape vehicle. [[Hapan Security]] officer [[Taryn Zel]] used the vehicle's [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]] to ward off pursuing [[Galactic Alliance Security|GAS]] speeders during the raid.<ref name="Vortex" />
